lithos_version: lithos 0.5.0 @ a4d2d62; every error envelope below probed against a live Lithos (MCP serverInfo 3.2.0, 2026-10-04) except where observed_divergences says otherwise

request.notes: Accepted types: `blocks` (to_task is not ready until from_task completes), `parent_child` (from_task is the parent; structural, never blocks), `discovered_from` (non-blocking) and `waits_on_gate` (to_task waits on the gate from_task). Both ids go through the shared resolver, whose domain is probed: a full id (>= 36 characters) goes to the edge write's own existence check, under six characters is `invalid_input`, a 6-to-35-character value is searched as a prefix and matching nothing is the resolver's `task_not_found` ("No task matches id prefix …") while matching several is `ambiguous_id_prefix` with up to FIVE `{id, title}` candidate records whose capped count the message states. Every message names WHICH argument failed (`from_task_id` / `to_task_id`), and `from_task_id` is resolved first — a request with two bad ids is refused for the first one. Validation order, probed: BOTH ids are resolved first (from, then to), then the edge type, then the self-edge check on the RESOLVED ids, then existence, then the type-specific rules (`not_a_gate`, `parent_exists`, `cycle`). So `("x", "x", "blocks")` is the resolver's `invalid_input` for `from_task_id`, not `self_edge`, and an unknown type with a too-short id is `invalid_input` too — an earlier pass of this slice recorded the reverse order as probed, wrongly. A `cycle` is refused over the blocking edges (`blocks` + `waits_on_gate`, a dependency cycle) and over `parent_child` (a hierarchy cycle); the message names the new edge and then the cycle by FULL id, rendered from the new edge's SOURCE along what each member depends on for a dependency cycle, and from its TARGET parent -> child for a hierarchy one. On an EXISTING (from, to, type) the call returns the same success payload as an insert, REPLACES that edge's metadata, and leaves `created_by` / `created_at` as they were — so those two fields are evidence of who inserted an edge, which is what T3 D11's removal offer rests on. An edge write emits NO event, which is why Lens re-reads the focal task's edges around the call and publishes its own synthetic `lens.edge_upserted`.

errors.message: edge type 'duplicates' is not accepted in this phase (accepted: ['blocks', 'discovered_from', 'parent_child', 'waits_on_gate']).
An edge cannot connect a task to itself.
from_task_id 'infl' is too short: pass the full task id or a prefix of at least 6 characters.
to_task_id 'infl' is too short: pass the full task id or a prefix of at least 6 characters.
Task id prefix '506155' (from_task_id) is ambiguous: 2 or more matches. Retry with a longer prefix or a full id from candidates.
a waits_on_gate edge requires the from_task (influx-ingest-cutover) to be a 'gate' task, got task_type='task'.
blocks edge influx-backfill -> influx-ingest-cutover would create a dependency cycle: influx-backfill -> influx-ingest-cutover -> influx-backfill
parent_child edge influx-backfill -> influx-epic would create a hierarchy cycle: influx-epic -> influx-backfill -> influx-epic
task influx-backfill already has a parent (influx-epic); a task may have at most one parent. Remove the existing parent_child edge (lithos_task_edge_delete) before re-parenting.

observed_divergences: The success payload is the same for an insert and for a metadata replacement, so NOTHING in it says which happened — the residual T3 D11 states, and the upstream ask (a `created` flag) it would close. Its four keys beside `success` are transcribed from the source (`upsert_task_edge`); the tool's own description only says "with the resolved endpoint ids + titles" without naming them, and the body cannot be probed without writing an edge into the operator's graph. `invalid_edge_type`, `self_edge`, both too-short `invalid_input` cases, both resolver-level `task_not_found` cases, the edge write's own `task_not_found` (which names BOTH missing endpoints), `ambiguous_id_prefix` (candidates are `{id, title}` records) and `not_a_gate` ARE probed live, as is the validation order. The candidate CAP of five and the count the ambiguity message quotes come from the source: the live corpus has no six-character prefix shared by three tasks, so a capped list cannot be provoked there. `cycle` (both kinds, one-hop and multi-hop) and `parent_exists` ARE now probed too, against real edges whose refusal writes nothing — an earlier pass composed their messages, and neither composed text was the server's. The relative ORDER of `parent_exists` and a hierarchy `cycle` is NOT probed (the live graph has no grandchild to test it on); the fake checks `parent_exists` first. The `parent_exists` text names `lithos_task_edge_delete`, a tool a4d2d62 does not have, so the pinned source's wording of that sentence necessarily differs — the code and the named parent are what Lens reads. The `cycle` message is rendered verbatim; Lens never parses it for logic. `invalid_edge_type` is treated as a Lens defect (the form offers only valid types). Probed 2026-10-04 against the live Lithos this environment reaches (MCP serverInfo 3.2.0). That server is NEWER than a4d2d62 — it serves `lithos_task_edge_delete`, which lithos-core `bd66d57c` added after 0.5.0 — and the Lithos source itself could not be read from this build environment, so where a message below is marked probed it is the live server's text, with ids substituted; a reviewer holding the a4d2d62 source should record any wording that differs there as a divergence here rather than replace the probed text.
